beats.subline: Friday, October 23, 2026 close — a choppy week in which Thursday's AI-spending selloff spread into other sectors before Friday's session steadied, leaving the Dow slightly higher and the S&P and Nasdaq slightly lower on net.
beats.body: Weak reactions to Tesla's and Meta's earnings reignited AI capital-spending worries midweek and hit consumer and healthcare names into Friday, while oil topped $116 a barrel on escalating US-Iran tensions; the Dow was the week's lone gainer, helped by a rotation into consumer staples and industrials.

beats.headline: Two IDF soldiers killed near Hebron prompt full West Bank lockdown
beats.body: Two Israeli soldiers were killed and five people wounded in an attack near Hebron Friday; Netanyahu ordered a full West Bank lockdown and convened an emergency security cabinet meeting over a feared follow-on attack, adding to a week of Mideast tension that has also pushed Brent crude above $116 a barrel on Strait of Hormuz fears tied to the US-Iran standoff.

beats.headline: No fresh news on this beat right now
beats.body: The most substantive item this week remains China's claim of 'indisputable sovereignty' over the Pratas Islands after a coast-guard standoff, which was already covered earlier this week; no genuinely new development surfaced within the 72-hour window.

beats.headline: Treasury says Gulf oil exports topped pre-war levels as US naval blockade squeezes Iran
beats.body: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Persian Gulf oil exports have recovered to roughly 17-18 million barrels a day, above pre-war levels, crediting the US naval blockade and sanctions campaign he calls Operation Economic Outcast with badly damaging Iran's oil revenue; CENTCOM separately released imagery of US F-16s refueling from a KC-135 over the Middle East as the standoff continues.

beats.body: No qualifying new military-technology development surfaced within the 72-hour window; this week's Pentagon-Lockheed F-35 framework was already covered in Friday's brief, and Space Force hypersonic-tracking satellite progress lacks a confirmed date within the window.

beats.headline: Anthropic donates its Agent Skills standard to a new Linux Foundation body
beats.body: Anthropic is donating Agent Skills, its open standard for giving AI agents specialized knowledge and workflows, to a newly formed Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation, transferring the name, logo, GitHub organization and agentskills.io domain to make it vendor-neutral and community-governed.
